message.content: Logistic regression is a statistical method used for binary classification problems. It models the probability that a given input belongs to one of two classes (e.g., “yes” vs. “no”) as a logistic function of a linear combination of the input features. In other words, it estimates the log‑odds of the outcome as a linear function of the predictors and then transforms those log‑odds back into probabilities using the logistic (sigmoid) function. The model parameters are typically estimated via maximum likelihood estimation, and the resulting probabilities can be thresholded to make class predictions.
